title: What Calendars Do Inside LeadProspectrr
learningGoal: Understand how calendars in LeadProspectrr replace back-and-forth scheduling messages with a simple booking link.

items.title: One Link Replaces Many Messages
items.description: Instead of asking 'What time works for you?' you send one booking link. The person chooses a time and LeadProspectrr handles the rest.

items.title: Automatic Confirmations
items.description: LeadProspectrr records the appointment, sends confirmations, and can send reminders before the meeting.

items.title: The Bridge to Conversation
items.description: The calendar is often the bridge between interest and a real conversation. A clean booking link removes friction.

items.title: Without a Booking Link
items.description: The consultant asks 'What days work for you?' The prospect replies later. Times are suggested. One time no longer works. The conversation slows down.

items.title: With a Booking Link
items.description: The consultant says 'Here is the link to choose a time that works for you.' The prospect books immediately. Cleaner, faster, easier for both sides.

keyPoint: A booking calendar turns scheduling from a conversation into a simple action. One link, one choice, one confirmed appointment.

options.option_text: Nothing happens until you manually confirm
LeadProspectrr records the appointment and can send confirmations and reminders
They are immediately charged a fee

quizzes.explanation: LeadProspectrr automatically records the appointment and can send confirmation emails and reminder messages before the meeting.

quizzes.question: Why is a booking link better than email scheduling?

options.option_text: It removes friction and lets people book immediately

quizzes.explanation: A booking link removes the back-and-forth of email scheduling, letting prospects book immediately while their interest is high.

title: Key Calendar Terms Made Simple
learningGoal: Learn the essential calendar vocabulary used in LeadProspectrr.

items.title: Calendar
items.description: The booking setup for one type of appointment. Think of it as a template for a specific meeting type.

items.title: Appointment
items.description: A meeting someone has booked. The actual event on your schedule.

items.title: Availability
items.description: The days and times people are allowed to book. You control when people can see open slots.

items.title: Buffer Time
items.description: Extra space before or after appointments. Breathing room for prep, notes, or travel.

items.title: Booking Link
items.description: The link people use to choose a time. Share this link anywhere you want people to book.

items.title: Confirmation
items.description: The message sent after someone books. Usually includes appointment details and calendar invite.

items.title: Reminder
items.description: The message sent before the appointment. Reduces no-shows by reminding people of upcoming meetings.

items.title: Connected Calendar
items.description: An outside calendar like Google or Outlook connected to LeadProspectrr to prevent double-booking.

items.title: Conflict Calendar
items.description: A calendar used to block unavailable times. Shows LeadProspectrr when you are already busy.

keyPoint: Understanding these terms helps you set up your calendar correctly and avoid common mistakes like double-booking or missing appointments.

actionSteps.title: Review the Terms
actionSteps.description: Read through each term and think about how it applies to your business.

actionSteps.title: Identify Your Needs
actionSteps.description: Which terms are most relevant to your current scheduling challenges?

actionSteps.description: Look for these terms in the LeadProspectrr calendar area to see them in context.

quizzes.question: What is 'availability' in calendar terms?

options.option_text: The days and times people are allowed to book
The number of appointments you can handle

quizzes.explanation: Availability refers to the specific days and times you make available for people to book appointments.

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of 'buffer time'?

options.option_text: To create space before or after appointments for prep, notes, or travel

quizzes.explanation: Buffer time creates breathing room between appointments so you have time to prepare, take notes, or travel to your next meeting.

quizzes.question: What does a 'conflict calendar' do?

options.option_text: Blocks unavailable times to prevent double-booking

quizzes.explanation: A conflict calendar shows LeadProspectrr when you are already busy, blocking those times from being booked to prevent double-booking.

title: The Simple Booking Flow
learningGoal: Understand the 10-step process for setting up and using a booking calendar.

items.title: 1. Create Calendar
items.description: Create a calendar in LeadProspectrr for a specific appointment type.

items.title: 2. Set Appointment Type
items.description: Define what kind of meeting this is: discovery call, strategy session, etc.

items.title: 3. Set Appointment Length
items.description: Choose how long the meeting will last: 15, 30, 45, or 60 minutes.

items.title: 4. Set Availability
items.description: Choose which days and times people can book.

items.title: 5. Add Buffer Time
items.description: Add breathing room before or after appointments if needed.

items.title: 6. Add Meeting Details
items.description: Specify phone, Zoom, Google Meet, or physical address.

items.title: 7. Set Confirmations and Reminders
items.description: Configure messages sent after booking and before appointments.

items.title: 8. Copy the Booking Link
items.description: Get your unique booking link to share with others.

items.title: 9. Share the Booking Link
items.description: Add the link to your email signature, website, or messages.

items.title: 10. Test the Process
items.description: Book a test appointment to make sure everything works.

keyPoint: The calendar should not confuse the person booking. They should know what they are booking, how long it takes, what happens after, where it happens, and how they will be reminded.

actionSteps.title: Review the Flow
actionSteps.description: Read through all 10 steps and identify which ones you need help with.

actionSteps.description: Navigate to LeadProspectrr calendars and locate each setting mentioned.

quizzes.question: What is the first step in the booking flow?
quizzes.explanation: The first step is to create a calendar in LeadProspectrr. You need a calendar before you can share a link or book appointments.

quizzes.question: Why is step 10 (Test the Process) important?

options.option_text: It is optional and can be skipped
It ensures everything works before real prospects use it

quizzes.explanation: Testing protects your business from looking unprofessional. It ensures confirmations, reminders, and meeting details all work correctly before real prospects use the link.

quizzes.question: What should someone know after viewing your booking page?

options.option_text: What they are booking, how long, what happens after, where, and how they will be reminded

quizzes.explanation: A good booking page clearly communicates what is being booked, duration, next steps, location, and reminder details so the person feels confident completing the booking.

title: Choose the Right Calendar Type
learningGoal: Understand the three types of calendars and when to use each one.

items.title: Start Here
items.description: For most clients, start with a simple Personal Booking Calendar for one-to-one appointments.

items.title: Good Examples
items.description: 15-Minute Intro Call, 30-Minute Discovery Call, 45-Minute Strategy Session, Client Check-In, Support Call.

items.title: Best For
items.description: Coaches, consultants, speakers, trainers, and anyone booking individual calls with prospects or clients.

items.title: When to Use
items.description: Use when the event itself is the focus, not one staff member's personal availability.

items.title: Good Examples
items.description: Clinic session, Workshop, Seminar, Group training, Public booking session.

items.title: Best For
items.description: Group events where multiple people book into the same session at a specific date and time.

items.title: When to Use
items.description: Use when booking a service, staff member, time slot, and possibly payment.

items.title: Good Examples
items.description: Paid consultation, Coaching session, Service appointment, Team-based service booking.

items.title: Best For
items.description: Businesses with multiple staff, services with different durations, or appointments requiring payment.

keyPoint: Start simple. Create the calendar that matches the most common booking you need right now. Do not build five calendars when one good calendar will solve the problem.

actionSteps.description: What is your most common appointment? One-on-one call, group event, or paid service?

quizzes.explanation: Most clients should start with a Personal Booking Calendar for one-to-one appointments like discovery calls or client check-ins.

quizzes.question: When should you use an Event Calendar?

options.option_text: When the event itself is the focus, like workshops or group training

quizzes.explanation: Use an Event Calendar when multiple people book into the same session, like workshops, seminars, or group training sessions.

quizzes.question: What is the simple rule for getting started?

options.option_text: Start simple with one calendar for your most common booking need
Create a new calendar for every prospect

quizzes.explanation: Start with one simple calendar that matches your most common booking need. You can always add more calendars later as your business grows.

title: Set Up a Basic Calendar
learningGoal: Learn the 10 steps to create and configure a working booking calendar.

items.title: 1. Go to Calendars
items.description: Inside LeadProspectrr, go to the calendar area and open calendar settings.

items.title: 2. Create or Edit
items.description: Choose to create a new calendar or edit an existing one. For training, use '30-Minute Discovery Call'.

items.title: 3. Name It Clearly
items.description: Good names: '30-Minute Discovery Call', 'Client Check-In', 'Strategy Session'. Poor names: 'Calendar 1', 'Test'.

items.title: 4. Set Appointment Length
items.description: Quick Intro: 15 min, Discovery: 30 min, Strategy: 45-60 min, Check-In: 15-30 min.

items.title: 5. Set Availability
items.description: Set days and times people can book. Consider working hours, lunch, admin time, and timezone.

items.title: 6. Add Buffer Time
items.description: Add breathing room: 10 min before to prepare, 15 min after for notes, 30 min between long meetings.

items.title: 7. Add Meeting Details
items.description: Specify phone, Zoom, Google Meet, or address. Make the next step crystal clear.

items.title: 8. Set Notifications
items.description: Configure confirmation email, reminder email, SMS reminder, and internal notifications.

items.title: 9. Save and Review
items.description: Check name, length, availability, location, reminders, timezone, and booking link before saving.

items.title: 10. Copy the Booking Link
items.description: Copy your unique booking link and prepare to test it before sharing.

keyPoint: A well-configured calendar removes all confusion. The person booking knows exactly what they are getting, when, where, and what happens next.

quizzes.explanation: Good calendar names are clear and descriptive, like '30-Minute Discovery Call' or 'Client Check-In', so prospects understand what they are booking.

quizzes.explanation: A standard discovery call is typically 30 minutes—long enough to understand needs but short enough to respect everyone's time.

quizzes.explanation: Before saving, review all settings: name, appointment length, availability, meeting location, reminders, timezone, and booking link to ensure everything is correct.

title: Connect Calendars and Reduce Double-Booking
learningGoal: Learn how to connect external calendars and prevent double-booking.

items.title: The Double-Booking Problem
items.description: If you have meetings in Google Calendar, Outlook, or other calendars, LeadProspectrr needs to know when you are busy.

items.title: The Solution
items.description: Connected calendars and conflict calendars show LeadProspectrr your real availability and block busy times.

items.title: Professional Protection
items.description: Preventing double-booking protects your reputation and avoids embarrassing scheduling conflicts.

items.title: Correct Calendar Connected?
items.description: Is the right external calendar (Google, Outlook) connected to LeadProspectrr?

items.title: Right Conflict Calendar?
items.description: Is the correct calendar being checked for conflicts and busy times?

items.title: Busy Times Blocking?
items.description: Are your busy times properly blocking appointment slots?

items.title: Bookings Syncing Back?
items.description: Are new bookings appearing on your external calendar if needed?

items.title: Timezone Correct?
items.description: Is the timezone setting correct for both calendars?

keyPoint: Double-booking usually happens when the calendar is not checking the real calendar where you already have meetings. Always connect your main calendar as a conflict calendar.

actionSteps.title: Identify Your Main Calendar
actionSteps.description: Where do you currently track meetings? Google Calendar? Outlook? Apple Calendar?

actionSteps.title: Connect Your Calendar
actionSteps.description: In LeadProspectrr, connect your main external calendar to prevent double-booking.

actionSteps.title: Set as Conflict Calendar
actionSteps.description: Make sure your connected calendar is set as a conflict calendar to block busy times.

actionSteps.title: Test the Connection
actionSteps.description: Create a test event on your external calendar and verify it blocks that time in LeadProspectrr.

quizzes.question: What usually causes double-booking?

options.option_text: The calendar not checking your real calendar where you already have meetings

quizzes.explanation: Double-booking happens when LeadProspectrr doesn't know about meetings on your external calendar. Connecting your main calendar as a conflict calendar prevents this.

quizzes.question: What is a conflict calendar?

options.option_text: A calendar used to block unavailable times and prevent double-booking

items.description: Verify reminder messages are scheduled correctly.

title: Common Mistakes and Better Options
learningGoal: Learn the most common calendar mistakes and how to avoid them.

items.title: Using One Calendar for Everything
items.description: Mistake: One calendar for all appointment types. Better: Create different calendars for different appointment types.

items.title: Leaving Availability Too Open
items.description: Mistake: Showing all hours. Better: Only show times you are happy for people to book.

items.title: No Reminders
items.description: Mistake: Skipping reminders. Better: Use email and/or SMS reminders to reduce no-shows.

items.title: Sharing Before Testing
items.description: Mistake: Sharing the link immediately. Better: Book a test appointment first.

items.title: Confusing Calendar Names
items.description: Mistake: Names like 'Calendar 1'. Better: Use names clients understand like 'Discovery Call'.

items.title: No Meeting Location
items.description: Mistake: Unclear meeting details. Better: Add phone, Zoom, Google Meet, or address details.

items.title: Wrong Timezone
items.description: Mistake: Incorrect timezone settings. Better: Check timezone before sharing the link.

items.title: No Conflict Calendar
items.description: Mistake: No external calendar connected. Better: Connect the calendar showing your real busy times.

keyPoint: Most calendar problems come from rushing the setup. Take time to configure properly, test thoroughly, and review regularly.

quizzes.question: What is a common mistake when setting up availability?

options.option_text: Leaving availability too open and showing times you don't want booked

quizzes.explanation: A common mistake is leaving availability too open, showing times you don't actually want people to book. Only show times you are truly available.

quizzes.question: Why should you avoid using one calendar for everything?

options.option_text: Different appointment types need different settings, lengths, and availability

quizzes.explanation: Different appointment types (discovery calls vs. client check-ins) need different lengths, availability, and settings. Separate calendars keep everything organized.

quizzes.question: What should you do before sharing your booking link?
quizzes.explanation: Always book a test appointment before sharing your link publicly. This ensures everything works correctly and protects your professional reputation.
